title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: One prior $12.03 week (2026-09-28) sold x0.70 vs baseline; post-promo dip (x0.76) suggests price sensitivity. No prior 6.2% increase seen, so shrink toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. A 6.2% price increase to $12.03 is a significant deterrent. Historical data shows price increases correlate with demand drops: the week after a 30% off promotion saw 24% below baseline (x0.76), and a prior $12.03 week (2026-09-28) sold 13 units (x0.70 vs baseline). The heatwave (38°C) may boost cold/flu relief demand, but this product is not typically seasonal for heat. No promotion or event is scheduled. The classical model’s x1.00 is overly optimistic given the price hike. Evidence points to a downside effect, shrunk toward 1.0 due to limited prior price change data. No noise-adjusted lift from heat is evident.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 4.5 - 37.5 | 10%-90%: 8.2 - 33.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
